header:
Meeting: Monarch Edge — Implementation Immersion Kickoff
Date: 2026-05-08
Time: 4:00 PM PT
Duration: 28 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ramiro Ortega (Redwood CSM), Alicia Chu (Monarch Edge), Ben Watkins (Monarch Edge), Diego Ramos (Monarch Edge SRE), Nadia Kim (Monarch Edge Product)
summary: Introductory implementation kickoff covering architecture decisions (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security requirements (KMS/SAML/SOC2), pilot scope and success criteria. Agreed to a short pilot and a technical deep dive to validate latency and quantization tradeoffs.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok great everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE for Monarch Edge, we also have priya our solutions engineer and ramiro our CSM.
[00:07] Alicia: hi yeah thanks, excited, we've been looking forward to getting started.
[00:12] Priya: hey all, quick agenda — architecture review, security intake, pilot definition, next steps. should be about 25, 30 minutes.
[00:22] Ben: sounds good. just so you know — our infra team is strict on VPC peering and we need to keep everything inside us-east-1 for now.
[00:30] Ramiro: noted — we'll call out region pinning in the runbook.
[00:34] Diego: also latency target — sub 80ms tail for chat flows, that's kind of our SLA.
[00:41] Priya: ok sub 80ms tail, noted. couple of clarifying q's: are those 80ms for single-turn or multi-turn with KV cache?
[00:49] Diego: primarily single-turn but we do multi-turn in user sessions, so both matter. and we want predictable tail behavior.
[00:56] Priya: got it. that steers us to consider dedicated capacity or private deployment for production; hosted for dev.
[01:03] Alicia: can you explain tradeoffs very quickly — i know you have hosted and dedicated and private.
[01:09] Jordan: yeah so high level — hosted is fastest to onboard but can have noisy neighbor variability, dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with backed throughput and SLA, private is for customers who need VPC-only control or on-prem for compliance.
[01:22] Ben: we are leaning dedicated because of the tail concerns, but we also need KMS integration and audit logs.
[01:29] Ramiro: we do offer KMS/HSM integrations and per-request audit logging; we'll put the exact docs in the security packet.
[01:36] Alicia: what's the typical quantization impact on performance — i've read some notes but want concrete numbers.
[01:41] Priya: short answer — 8-bit/4-bit quantization reduces memory and can improve throughput but may slightly affect answer quality. for many retrieval-augmented chat use cases it's fine; priya: we'll run a quick perf+quality sweep in the deep dive. (laughter)
[01:57] Ben: ok that sounds reasonable. how do we run a perf test — do you need us to share prompt sets?
[02:03] Priya: yes share prompt sets and token distribution. Alicia, if you can share a representative 200-300 prompt sample and typical sequence lengths we can run bench with your data.
[02:13] Alicia: yep i'll pull a sample. expect that by monday.
[02:16] Diego: on networking — we have corporate firewalling and strict egress rules, we might need peering and a narrow CIDR list.
[02:24] Jordan: understood — we'll include the VPC peering checklist and minimal CIDR ranges; also note we support private control planes for stricter networks.
[02:31] Nadia: on compliance, do you have SOC 2 docs? our legal is asking.
[02:35] Ramiro: yes we have SOC 2 and ISO artefacts; i'll send those links. also SAML SSO and RBAC are supported.
[02:42] Ben: any enterprise onboarding costs or minimums for Dedicated?
[02:46] Jordan: there's a reserved capacity contract typically monthly/annual; for pilot we can spin up a small dedicated pool or run on hosted with capacity reservation. i'll include cost bands in the follow up.
[02:58] Alicia: success criteria — for pilot we want: sustained 100k tokens/day, average p95 latency under 80ms on representative prompts, integration with our KMS and SAML, and no PII leakage in logs.
[03:14] Priya: good success criteria. we'll map those to acceptance tests.
[03:19] Ben: timeline — we'd like pilot in 2 weeks if possible.
[03:23] Jordan: tight but doable; action items: runbook sent by Monday, Ramiro to provision trial tenant by Tue/Wed, Priya to schedule perf deep dive by next Thursday.
[03:34] Diego: a quick question — how do rollouts work; can we do canary and fallback?
[03:39] Priya: yes rollouts support canary/A-B and automatic fallback to model variants or older versions. matches product docs.
[03:46] Alicia: any known gaps with our stack? we run k8s internal endpoints and some proprietary retriever.
[03:53] Priya: sounds compatible — we'll need to validate retriever latency and embedding sizes; for embeddings we support vector sizes up to 2048 but we typically recommend smaller dims.
[04:05] Ben: who will be our day-to-day contact?
[04:08] Ramiro: i'll be primary CSM for the onboarding and runbook; Jordan for contract/pricing; Priya for SE deep dives.
[04:15] Jordan: ok next steps recap: i'll send runbook + pricing bands + region/VPC checklist; priya will propose times for perf deep dive and bench plan; ramiro will provision test tenant and share trial access; alicia will share prompt samples and typical token distributions.
[04:30] Alicia: thanks all, that works.
[04:32] Diego: one more thing — logging retention and whether logs are searchable in the console.
[04:36] Ramiro: we have configurable retention; search is in the console and we can export logs to your S3 or SIEM. we'll include retention options in the docs.
[04:45] Ben: fine. thanks everyone.
[04:47] Jordan: great — we'll follow up with the packet. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional filler words, a few mis-recognized product names (example: "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache"), small speaker attribution jitter (some lines labeled by role rather than name).
